note: Slugs are pattern.monster's own. `tile` is how wide one repeat is drawn on the 1024 artboard; `ink` is the stroke weight in artboard units. `rows` only means anything for the patterns whose tile stacks rows of the same shape, and says how many to keep. `tile` runs from about 195 to 290 artboard units, against an egg roughly 640 wide before the crop — so a surface shows a handful of repeats rather than a mesh. Under about 180 the tile stops being a texture you can see and becomes noise at icon size; over about 300 one repeat fills the smallest egg in a trio and that egg loses its surface. Everything here is a surface — a grid, a hatch, a wave, a contour, a speckle, a scale, a tessellation. Nothing decorative: no zigzag bands, no flowers, no plaid, no stars, no big spots. Those are what make an egg read as an Easter egg.
